name: Double-Under
description: The double-under is an advanced jump rope skill in which the rope passes under the feet twice in a single jump, requiring a higher jump and faster rope rotation than a standard single-under. It significantly elevates the cardiovascular demand over single-unders, while also training rope timing, wrist speed, and the explosive ankle and calf plantarflexion needed to achieve sufficient jump height. Double-unders are a standard exercise in competitive functional fitness.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright with the jump rope behind the heels, one handle in each hand.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a speed rope with handles appropriate for double-under rotation. The rope should be slightly shorter than used for single-unders.
steps: Step 1: Begin with a standard single-under rhythm to establish timing.
Step 2: On a chosen jump, explode upward more powerfully than a single-under to achieve greater jump height.
Step 3: Simultaneously accelerate wrist rotation to pass the rope under the feet twice before landing.
Step 4: Land softly on the balls of the feet with slightly bent knees.
Step 5: Return to the standard rhythm or continue consecutive double-unders.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously. The higher metabolic demand requires efficient breathing rhythm.
common_mistakes: Piking the hips — kicking the heels back instead of jumping straight up
Moving the arms wide to slow the rope — wrists should do the work
Panicking and breaking rhythm — stay composed and consistent
safety_considerations: High Achilles and calf demand — do not progress volume too rapidly.
Master single-unders and consistent rhythm before attempting.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Enough jump height for the rope to pass twice — typically 10–15 cm off the floor.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Typically programmed in sets of 50–100 reps unbroken, or for time intervals.
coaching_cues: Flick the wrist fast — not the arms
Stay relaxed and trust the rhythm
